# Results — Study 873 (Sentiment Beta)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Baker
& Wurgler (2006, 2007): the stocks whose returns **co-move most with market sentiment**
(high *sentiment beta*) are the speculative names that get over-priced in euphoria and
**under-perform afterwards**, so a long-low-beta / short-high-beta book should earn a
positive spread. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the
partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `357fd262912f` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Sentiment gauge | a **tradable high-minus-low-vol spread** built from the panel: daily return of the top-30% by trailing-63-day vol (speculative) minus the bottom-30% (safe). Mean **+4.74 bps/day**, ann-vol **19.4%**, lag-1 autocorr **−0.007** (real data — one of the two proxies the brief names) |
| Signal | each name's **252-day sentiment beta** = rolling OLS slope of its daily return on the gauge (`cov/var`), known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by the beta; **long the bottom 30%** (low sentiment beta), **short the top 30%** (high sentiment beta), equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled low-vs-high books; a post-peak conditional cut; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |
| Sample window | as-of 2026-06-30 (last complete calendar month; partial current month dropped); Fingerprint `357fd262912f` |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. Crucially,
the Baker-Wurgler sentiment-beta premium is documented as a **hard-to-value / hard-to-arbitrage
small-and-speculative-stock** effect; a 50-mega-cap survivor panel is exactly where it is
*least* likely to appear — which is what we find.

## The headline — long-low-beta / short-high-beta spread

Daily equal-weight bottom-30% minus top-30% sentiment-beta spread (n = **3,831** days):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long low-beta − short high-beta)** | **−6.20 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **−2.86** |
| one-sample *t* | −2.77 |
| low-beta book / high-beta book | +4.82 bps / +11.01 bps (Welch *t* = −2.05) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | −0.71 |

The claimed edge **fails to replicate — and inverts.** Baker-Wurgler predict a *positive*
long-low/short-high spread (the high-sentiment-beta euphoria-chasers under-earn); on this
mega-cap universe the spread is **significantly negative** (−6.20 bps/day, NW *t* = −2.86):
the **high**-sentiment-beta names — the momentum tech mega-caps whose returns sync with the
speculative leg — actually *out-earned* the boring low-beta ones over 2010–2026. The
sentiment-beta premium is a speculative-small-stock phenomenon that does not survive on 50
mega-caps.

## Conditional — is it stronger after sentiment peaks?

The claim says the under-performance is sharpest *after sentiment has peaked*. Split the spread
by the trailing level of the gauge (top-30% of the 252-day gauge level = a high-sentiment regime):

| regime | spread | NW *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| high-sentiment (after peaks) | **−9.21 bps** | −2.48 | 1,150 |
| the rest | −4.91 bps | −1.86 | 2,681 |

The *conditioning* works — the effect **is** larger after sentiment peaks — but with the
**reversed** sign: after euphoria the high-beta names out-earned by *more*, not less. The
"post-peak amplification" is real; its direction is the opposite of the theory here.

## Placebo — is the (reversed) relation a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the sentiment-beta sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted**
panel (signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **−6.20 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +0.004 bps (1.317) |
| position of observed | ≈ **4.71σ into the left tail** (right-tail p = 1.000 ⇒ left-tail p ≈ 0.000) |

The permutation null centres at zero; the observed −6.20 bps sits far in the **left** tail, so
the (opposite-sign) relation is real and not a lucky sort — the sign is simply the reverse of
the literature's on this universe.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,697) | −4.45 bps | −1.73 |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | −7.59 bps | **−2.29** |

The reversal is present in both halves (and significant in the recent one); the early era is
directionally the same but below the |t|≥2 bar. Either way there is **no** era in which the
*claimed* (positive) premium appears.

## The timer — can you get paid for it (either direction)?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | −6.20 bps | 2.14 bps | **−8.34 bps** | −3.73 | −0.96 | −21.0%/yr |
| **5 bps** | −6.20 bps | 10.14 bps | **−16.34 bps** | −7.30 | −1.87 | −41.2%/yr |

The specified book loses money gross; and even the *sign-flipped* book (long high-beta) would
earn only +6.20 bps/day gross from a heavily factor-exposed long-short — which the 2.14 bps/day
round-trip friction at a mere 1 bp already eats a third of, and which carries the speculative
leg's ≈19% vol. **Mirage** either way.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel: a common sentiment factor with dispersed per-name loadings (the true
betas); with `edge>0` a high loading depresses the name's forward mean. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.05** (sd 0.94), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.0025`, seed 873) | **+5.86** (Welch *t* = +8.13) |

The detector recovers a *planted* Baker-Wurgler relation cleanly and never fires on the null — so
the negative real-tape result is a genuine sign-reversal on the mega-cap universe, not a bug.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The famous Baker-Wurgler sentiment-beta premium does **not** replicate on
  50 liquid US mega-caps. The specified long-low-beta / short-high-beta spread is **−6.20 bps/day**
  (NW *t* = **−2.86**) — significant but *opposite in sign* to the claim, ≈4.71σ into the left tail
  of a 1,000-permutation placebo, with a clean 20-seed synthetic control. The claimed edge is
  absent (it is a speculative-small-stock phenomenon); on mega-caps the high-beta names out-earned,
  and *more so* after sentiment peaked.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The specified book loses money gross and net (−8.34 bps/day at 1 bp,
  −16.34 at 5 bps); even the data-mined sign-flip is a factor-exposed ≈19%-vol book whose gross
  edge the round-trip friction at 1 bp already erodes.
